title: Harvard LEAD Fellowship 2027–2028: Fully Funded Global Health Leadership Fellowship for Professionals from Low- and Middle-Income Countries
summary: The 2027–2028 Harvard LEAD Fellowship for Promoting Women in Global Health is now accepting applications for professionals seeking to strengthen their leadership capacity and make a greater impact in global health. Offered by the Harvard Global Health Institute (HGHI) in collaboration with the Department of Global Health and Population at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health , the LEAD Fellowship is a one-year programme designed to support the continued development of established and emerging leaders in global health. The fellowship is particularly structured to provide participants with time, mentorship, coaching, executive education, networking and reflection to help them advance their leadership goals. The fellowship provides a highly personalized leadership development experience rather than relying solely on conventional classroom-based training. Fellows have the opportunity to work with Harvard faculty and senior mentors while developing a leadership curriculum tailored to their individual interests, professional goals and areas for growth. For the 2027–2028 cohort, the fellowship will combine a 12-month virtual curriculum with a six-week in-person experience in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in spring 2028 . Applications for the fellowship must be submitted by 11:59 PM EST on Sunday, November 15, 2026 . What Is the Harvard LEAD Fellowship? The Harvard LEAD Fellowship is a one-year leadership development programme for professionals working in global health. The programme is offered through the Harvard Global Health Institute in collaboration with the Department of Global Health and Population at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. Its central purpose is to strengthen leadership among professionals who are already contributing to global health and who demonstrate the potential to take on greater leadership responsibilities. The programme takes a highly individualized approach to leadership development. Rather than requiring every participant to follow exactly the same professional development pathway, fellows are given the opportunity to build a curriculum around their own: Professional interests Leadership goals Areas of expertise Areas requiring further development Long-term ambitions Global health priorities This personalized structure allows fellows to use the programme to address the leadership challenges most relevant to their own professional circumstances. A One-Year Leadership Development Experience The 2027–2028 LEAD Fellowship will run for one year, from: September 1, 2027, to August 31, 2028. During this period, fellows will participate in a 12-month virtual curriculum combined with a six-week in-person experience in spring 2028 . The in-person component is scheduled for April 2028 and requires fellows to reside in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA, for six weeks . The combination of virtual learning and in-person engagement allows participants to remain connected to the programme throughout the fellowship year while also benefiting from an intensive period of direct interaction with Harvard faculty, mentors and other fellows. What Does the Harvard LEAD Fellowship Include? The programme provides a broad range of leadership development opportunities. Throughout the fellowship year, participants will engage in: One-on-one leadership coaching Mentorship An executive education course Speaking events Private leadership masterclasses led by Harvard faculty Networking opportunities Tailored leadership training Independent project work Cohort-based learning Interaction with senior mentors and Harvard faculty These components are designed to provide fellows with both structured leadership education and opportunities for personal reflection and professional exploration. One-on-One Leadership Coaching Individual coaching is one of the important components of the LEAD Fellowship. Rather than treating leadership development as a one-size-fits-all process, the programme connects fellows with support tailored to their individual leadership needs. One-on-one coaching can provide participants with dedicated space to examine their professional experiences, leadership challenges, goals and areas for further development. For experienced global health professionals who are already managing demanding responsibilities, this dedicated opportunity for reflection can be particularly valuable. Mentorship from Experienced Leaders Fellows are connected with mentors who provide guidance aligned with their individual goals. The mentorship component allows participants to benefit from the experience and perspectives of established professionals while thinking more deliberately about their own leadership development. The programme also connects fellows with world-class Harvard faculty and senior mentors. This creates opportunities for participants to learn from individuals with substantial experience in global health, leadership, research, policy and related areas. Executive Education and Harvard Masterclasses The fellowship includes an executive education course as well as private leadership masterclasses led by Harvard faculty. These opportunities provide fellows with structured exposure to advanced leadership concepts and ideas relevant to their professional development. The masterclasses are also designed to complement the individualized elements of the programme by giving participants access to Harvard faculty in a more focused setting. Speaking and Networking Opportunities The programme includes speaking events and networking opportunities throughout the fellowship year. These activities allow fellows to share perspectives, engage with other professionals and expand their networks. The cohort itself becomes an important source of professional exchange because participants come from different countries, professional backgrounds and areas of global health. According to the programme, the LEAD Fellowship has already welcomed 26 fellows from 21 countries across Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe and South America . Past fellows have worked across areas including: Research Advocacy Administration Policy Clinical work The diversity of professional experiences is an important part of the fellowship s learning environment. A Global Network of Fellows and Alumni Participants become part of a growing community of LEAD Fellowship alumni. The programme describes the fellowship community as a close-knit network of former fellows from around the world. This network can provide opportunities for: Peer learning Professional networking Mentorship Collaboration Exchange of ideas Continued relationships beyond the fellowship year For global health professionals working across different countries and sectors, maintaining relationships with an international network of peers can be valuable for future collaborations and initiatives. Six-Week In-Person Experience at Harvard A defining component of the 2027–2028 fellowship is the six-week in-person experience in Cambridge, Massachusetts . Fellows are required to take a leave of absence, or an equivalent arrangement, from their home institution during this period. The in-person component provides an opportunity for fellows to step away temporarily from their regular professional responsibilities and dedicate concentrated time to leadership development. The fellowship describes this period as an opportunity for participants to reflect, recalibrate and explore new directions. When Will the In-Person Experience Take Place? The six-week in-residence experience will take place in April 2028 . Applicants must therefore be able to obtain the appropriate J-1 visa and be available to reside in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the required six-week period. Fellowship Support for the Harvard Residency The fellowship provides significant support for the required U.S. residency. According to the programme information: Visa fees will be covered. Housing will be covered. Flights will be covered. A living stipend will be provided for the period in the United States. This support is designed to enable selected fellows to participate in the in-person Harvard experience without having to bear the major costs associated with international travel and temporary residence in the United States. Who Is the Harvard LEAD Fellowship Designed For? The programme welcomes applicants from all continents, regions, disciplines, sectors and gender identities . However, applicants must meet several specific professional and academic requirements. The fellowship is intended for established global health professionals who already have substantial experience and leadership responsibilities. It is therefore not designed as an entry-level programme for recent graduates or individuals just beginning their professional careers. Academic Requirement Applicants must hold at least a Master s degree in a relevant field . The fellowship therefore expects candidates to have completed postgraduate education before applying. The relevant field should be connected to the applicant s global health work or professional background. Professional Experience Requirement Applicants must work full-time in the field of global health . In addition, candidates must have at least 10 years of professional experience beyond their education . An important clarification is that work completed while an individual was a university student does not count toward the required professional experience. Applicants should therefore calculate their professional experience based on work undertaken after completing their education rather than simply counting the number of years since they entered university. Leadership Experience and Potential The programme requires applicants to demonstrate substantial leadership experience as well as potential for further leadership development. This means candidates should be able to demonstrate more than technical expertise in global health. Strong applicants are likely to be professionals who can show evidence of leadership responsibilities, influence, programme development, policy engagement, institutional work, research leadership, advocacy or other forms of meaningful professional leadership. The fellowship is intended to help experienced professionals reflect on their existing leadership and develop new approaches for their future work. Leave of Absence Requirement Because the fellowship includes a six-week in-person experience in Cambridge, Massachusetts, applicants must be able to take a leave of absence or equivalent arrangement from their home institution during the residency in April 2028. This is an important requirement for professionals who currently hold full-time positions. Applicants should therefore consider their employer s policies and determine whether they can obtain the necessary time away from their regular responsibilities if selected. J-1 Visa and U.S. Residency Requirement Applicants must be eligible to obtain a J-1 visa for travel to the United States in April 2028. They must also be available to live in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for six weeks during the in-person portion of the programme. The fellowship will cover the visa fees, housing and flights associated with this experience, while also providing a living stipend for the period in the United States. Previous Fellowship Restriction Applicants should also consider their participation in other full-time fellowship programmes. The eligibility requirements state that, during the two years before their fellowship at Harvard , candidates may not have participated in another full-time fellowship lasting four months or longer . This restriction is important for applicants who have recently completed another substantial fellowship. Candidates should review their recent fellowship history carefully before applying. Gender and Geographic Inclusivity Despite the programme s title, applicants should note that the fellowship information explicitly states that applications are welcomed from all continents, regions, disciplines, sectors and gender identities . The programme has previously brought together fellows from Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe and South America. The fellowship s international orientation is reflected in the diversity of its existing alumni community, which includes professionals from 21 countries. Why the Harvard LEAD Fellowship Is Different The LEAD Fellowship differs from many traditional academic programmes because it emphasizes leadership development rather than simply academic instruction . Participants are already experienced global health professionals. The programme therefore focuses on giving fellows time and space to think deeply about their leadership, professional direction and future contribution to global health. Rather than simply adding another qualification to a professional résumé, the fellowship is designed to encourage fellows to step back from their daily responsibilities and reconsider how they can expand their impact. Personalized Leadership Development One of the strongest features of the fellowship is its customized approach. Each fellow has the autonomy to develop a leadership curriculum around their own: Professional interests Leadership objectives Career goals Areas for improvement Professional challenges Future ambitions This means two fellows may have very different fellowship experiences depending on their professional backgrounds and development priorities. The personalized model can be particularly useful for experienced professionals who have already developed technical expertise but want to strengthen their leadership capacity. Opportunities for Reflection and Professional Growth The fellowship places significant emphasis on reflection. Professionals working in global health often operate in demanding environments, balancing research, clinical work, policy responsibilities, administration, advocacy and other professional obligations. The LEAD Fellowship creates structured time for fellows to step away from those daily demands and think about their longer-term direction. The programme specifically seeks to provide fellows with the opportunity to: Reflect on their leadership journey Recalibrate their professional goals Connect with other global health leaders Explore new ideas Identify areas for growth Consider new directions Develop independent projects This reflective component is an important part of the programme s leadership philosophy. Benefits of Joining the Harvard LEAD Fellowship Selected fellows can benefit from a combination of academic, professional and leadership opportunities. Leadership Development Fellows receive customized leadership training, coaching and mentorship designed around their individual needs. Harvard Faculty Engagement Participants gain opportunities to interact with Harvard faculty through masterclasses, executive education and other programme activities. Senior Mentorship Senior mentors provide guidance and perspectives relevant to fellows individual leadership goals. International Networking Fellows join a global community of professionals working across different regions and areas of global health. Professional Reflection The programme provides dedicated time and space for participants to reassess their professional direction and leadership priorities. In-Person Harvard Experience Participants spend six weeks in Cambridge, Massachusetts, during spring 2028. Financial Support for the U.S. Residency The fellowship covers flights, housing and visa fees and provides a living stipend during the U.S. residency. Long-Term Alumni Network After completing the programme, fellows become part of the growing LEAD alumni community. Learn More HERE Application Deadline for the Harvard LEAD Fellowship 2027–2028 The application deadline is: Sunday, November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST. Applicants should ensure that all application materials are submitted before the stated deadline. Because the fellowship is highly competitive and requires substantial professional and leadership experience, prospective applicants should begin preparing well before the deadline rather than waiting until the final days. What Happens After Applying? Applicants selected for the fellowship will be notified in spring 2027 . The selected fellows will then participate in the fellowship programme from: September 1, 2027, through August 31, 2028. The fellowship year will combine virtual programming with the six-week in-person Harvard experience in April 2028. Timeline at a Glance Stage Date Applications open October 2026 Application deadline November 15, 2026 Selection notification Spring 2027 Fellowship begins September 1, 2027 Virtual fellowship curriculum September 2027–August 2028 Six-week Harvard residency April 2028 Fellowship ends August 31, 2028 How to Prepare a Strong Application Prospective applicants should approach the application strategically. 1. Review the Eligibility Requirements Before applying, confirm that you meet the minimum Master s degree, professional experience, full-time global health employment and leadership requirements. 2. Clearly Demonstrate Leadership Experience Applicants should be able to explain how they have demonstrated leadership throughout their careers. This may include leadership in: Global health programmes Research Policy Clinical settings Advocacy Administration Institutions Community initiatives Professional organizations 3. Explain Your Future Leadership Potential The fellowship is not only interested in what candidates have already accomplished. Applicants should also demonstrate how the LEAD Fellowship could help them grow and what they hope to accomplish in the future. 4. Identify Your Development Needs Because the fellowship is highly personalized, applicants should think carefully about the leadership areas in which they want to develop. Candidates should be prepared to explain what they hope to learn, explore or change during the fellowship. 5. Plan for the Six-Week Residency Applicants must be able to spend six weeks in Cambridge in April 2028. Before applying, candidates should consider their professional commitments, employer arrangements, visa eligibility and personal circumstances. 6. Start Early The November 15, 2026 deadline should be treated as a firm deadline. Applicants should give themselves sufficient time to review the official fellowship requirements, prepare their application materials and ensure that everything is submitted correctly. The Harvard LEAD Fellowship may be particularly relevant to experienced professionals who are already working in global health and want to strengthen their leadership capacity. Potential applicants may come from different areas of the global health ecosystem, including: Global health research Public health Health policy Healthcare administration Clinical work Health advocacy Global health programme management Health systems International development Academic and research institutions Government and policy institutions Non-governmental organizations The programme s previous fellows have worked across research, advocacy, administration, policy and clinical work, demonstrating the diversity of professional backgrounds represented in the fellowship community. A Global Opportunity for Experienced Health Leaders The LEAD Fellowship is particularly significant because it brings together experienced professionals from different countries and professional sectors. The programme has already welcomed 26 fellows from 21 countries across Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe and South America . This international composition allows participants to exchange perspectives on the challenges facing health systems and global health institutions in different settings. For professionals working in low- and middle-income countries, the opportunity can provide exposure to a global network while allowing them to develop leadership skills that can be applied within their own institutions and communities. Visit HERE for more information about the Harvard LEAD Fellowship for Promoting Women in Global Health 2027–2028 Conclusion The Harvard LEAD Fellowship for Promoting Women in Global Health 2027–2028 offers an intensive leadership development experience for experienced global health professionals seeking to expand their influence and effectiveness. Its combination of one-on-one coaching, senior mentorship, Harvard faculty engagement, executive education, leadership masterclasses, networking, independent project work and international peer learning creates a comprehensive professional development experience. The six-week in-person experience in Cambridge, Massachusetts, further distinguishes the programme by giving fellows dedicated time to step away from their regular professional responsibilities and focus on leadership development. Financial support for the residency, including flights, housing, visa fees and a living stipend, also helps make the international experience more accessible to selected fellows. Applicants should remember that this is an advanced professional fellowship. Candidates need at least a Master s degree in a relevant field, full-time employment in global health, at least 10 years of professional experience beyond their education, substantial leadership experience and demonstrated potential for further leadership development . The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST . Applicants who meet the requirements and are interested in strengthening their leadership contribution to global health should begin preparing their applications early and carefully review the official LEAD Fellowship requirements before submitting. title: DAAD In-Country/In-Region Scholarships 2026–2027: Fully Funded Master’s Opportunities for Sub-Saharan African Students
summary: The DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2026–2027 is offering scholarship opportunities for graduates and postgraduate students from Sub-Saharan Africa who wish to pursue selected development-related Master’s degree programmes within Africa. Funded by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) , the programme is designed to strengthen higher education systems across Sub-Saharan Africa by supporting talented graduates who have the potential to contribute to teaching, research and sustainable development in African higher education institutions. Unlike scholarships that require students to relocate to Europe or another distant region, the DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme enables successful applicants to undertake their Master’s studies within their home country or elsewhere in Sub-Saharan Africa , depending on the scholarship route and the applicant’s circumstances. For the 2026–2027 application cycle, a number of development-related Master’s programmes are currently open across countries including Burkina Faso, Ghana, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda and Malawi . The programme particularly encourages applications from women, recognised refugees, and candidates from marginalised regions or groups. Application Deadline: November 12, 2026 What Is the DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme? The DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa is a scholarship initiative aimed at developing strong, internationally oriented higher education systems in Africa. The programme recognises that sustainable development depends not only on financial resources and infrastructure but also on the availability of highly trained professionals, researchers and university educators who can contribute to knowledge production and capacity development within Africa. Through the programme, scholarships are awarded for selected development-related Master’s degree programmes . The broader objective is to support individuals who intend to build careers in teaching and/or research at higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa . This makes the scholarship particularly relevant for graduates who want to develop advanced academic and professional expertise while remaining connected to African higher education systems. What Does In-Country and In-Region Mean? The programme provides two main study possibilities. 1. In-Country Scholarship An In-Country scholarship allows an eligible applicant to pursue a Master’s degree: In their home country; or In a country where they already hold a valid residence permit. For example, a qualified Ghanaian applicant may pursue an eligible Master’s programme at one of the participating universities in Ghana. 2. In-Region Scholarship An In-Region scholarship supports applicants who wish to pursue an eligible Master’s degree in another Sub-Saharan African country outside their home country and outside a country in which they hold a residence permit. This creates an opportunity for African students to benefit from specialised academic programmes offered by universities elsewhere in the region. The distinction between In-Country and In-Region scholarships is therefore important because applicants should carefully examine the specific call for applications associated with the degree programme they intend to pursue. What Does the DAAD Scholarship Support? The scholarship supports selected development-related Master’s degree programmes . The programmes available under the current call cover a diverse range of fields, including: Water and environmental engineering Seed science and technology Molecular cell biology of infectious diseases Agricultural economics Environmental health Plant breeding Education research Electrical power systems Geomatics Climate change and disaster management Aquaculture and fisheries science Irrigation engineering The availability of a particular programme depends on the participating institution and the current application call. Applicants should therefore not assume that every university or degree programme in Sub-Saharan Africa is covered by the DAAD scholarship. The programme specifically supports the degree programmes listed in the relevant calls for applications. DAAD Scholarship Benefits The financial support provided through the DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme is designed to help successful scholars complete their Master s studies. Generally, scholarship support includes: Monthly Scholarship Successful scholars receive a monthly scholarship allowance to support them during their studies. The exact amount is determined according to the applicable scholarship regulations and the specific call for applications. Study and Research Allowance The scholarship generally provides a study and research allowance , helping scholars meet eligible academic and research-related expenses associated with their Master s programme. Thesis Publishing Costs The programme also provides support for thesis publishing costs , which can be particularly important for Master s students completing research-based degrees. Tuition Fees The scholarship includes support for tuition fees where applicable under the programme. Additional Benefits for In-Region Scholars Applicants receiving an In-Region scholarship may additionally receive: A travel allowance Health insurance The exact value and conditions of the benefits should be confirmed in the specific call for applications for the selected degree programme. Learn More HERE How Long Does the DAAD Scholarship Last? Funding is generally provided for the regular duration of the Master s programme , which is normally up to two years . This means that applicants should carefully review the duration of their intended degree programme and the specific funding conditions contained in its corresponding call for applications. The scholarship is intended to support scholars throughout the normal period required to complete the Master s programme rather than providing a short-term academic grant. Available DAAD Master’s Programmes for 2026–2027 The current DAAD scholarship database lists a number of participating universities and degree programmes whose application periods are currently open. These opportunities are distributed across several regions of Sub-Saharan Africa. West and Central Africa Burkina Faso Institut International d Ingenierie de l Eau et de l Environnement (2iE) Applicants can apply for: Master of Science in Water and Environmental Engineering This programme is particularly relevant to applicants interested in water resources, environmental management, engineering and sustainable development. Malawi University of Business and Applied Sciences (MUBAS) Available programme: Master of Science in Environmental Health Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources (LUANAR) Available programmes: Master of Science in Aquaculture and Fisheries Science Master of Science in Irrigation Engineering These programmes cover important areas related to food production, natural-resource management, water management, agriculture and sustainable development. Additional Programmes Expected to Open in 2027 The DAAD scholarship database also identifies several programmes whose calls are not currently open but are expected to be published in spring 2027 . These include programmes in Nigeria and South Africa. Nigeria Federal University of Agriculture Abeokuta (FUNAAB) Expected programme: Master of Science in Physics South Africa University of Cape Town (UCT) Expected programme: Master of Philosophy in Urban Studies – Southern Urbanism University of Pretoria (UP) Expected programme: Master of Science in Mathematics Applicants interested in these programmes should monitor the relevant university and DAAD announcements for the publication of their calls. Who Should Consider Applying? The DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme is particularly relevant to graduates and postgraduate applicants from Sub-Saharan Africa who have already obtained a first academic degree and want to undertake a development-related Master s degree. The programme is especially suited to people who see postgraduate education as preparation for careers in: University teaching Academic research Higher education leadership Agricultural research Environmental research Climate and disaster management Engineering Public health and environmental health Education research Science and technology Sustainable development The programme is also designed to contribute to the long-term strengthening of African higher education institutions. Applicants should therefore consider not only whether they meet the academic requirements of a particular Master s programme, but also whether their academic and professional aspirations align with the broader development objectives of the scholarship. Women and Applicants from Marginalised Groups Are Encouraged to Apply The DAAD specifically states that certain groups are especially encouraged to apply . These include: Female applicants Refugees with recognised refugee status Candidates from marginalised regions Candidates from marginalised groups This encouragement reflects the programme s broader goal of improving access to advanced education and strengthening higher education capacity across Sub-Saharan Africa. However, applicants should still meet the academic and programme-specific requirements established by the relevant university and scholarship call. How the Selection Process Works The selection procedure is not necessarily identical for every participating programme. The DAAD states that: The selection process differs between the individual degree programmes. This means applicants should not rely on a single universal selection procedure for every university. The relevant university s individual call for applications should be carefully reviewed because it contains the programme-specific application instructions and selection information. The application process may also differ depending on the region and host institution. For this reason, applicants should identify their preferred degree programme first and then read the corresponding call for applications before submitting their application. Important Application Considerations Applicants should pay close attention to the specific requirements of their chosen programme. The DAAD scholarship database provides an overview of the opportunities, but the detailed calls for applications contain the programme-specific information applicants need to make a complete application. Before applying, prospective scholars should therefore: Identify the Master s programme that matches their academic background and career goals. Confirm that the programme is currently accepting applications. Read the specific DAAD call for applications linked to that programme. Check the academic and admission requirements. Review the application procedure of the host university. Prepare all required documents. Follow the university-specific submission instructions. Submit the application before the stated deadline. Applicants should also pay attention to the distinction between In-Country and In-Region scholarships because this can affect where they are eligible to study. Why This Scholarship Matters for Sub-Saharan Africa The DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme is more than an individual scholarship opportunity. At a broader level, it is designed to strengthen African higher education systems by developing individuals who can contribute to teaching and research. This is important because universities and research institutions require highly trained academics and professionals capable of producing knowledge that responds to local and regional development challenges. By supporting Master s education within Sub-Saharan Africa, the programme also contributes to strengthening regional academic networks and reducing the need for all African postgraduate students to seek advanced training outside the continent. The range of supported disciplines further demonstrates the programme s development-oriented character. Fields such as climate change, environmental health, agricultural economics, plant breeding, water engineering, electrical power systems and disaster management address major development challenges facing African societies. Application Deadline The application deadline for the currently listed DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme opportunities is: November 12, 2026 Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin the application process. Because the application procedures can vary between participating universities, prospective applicants should review the relevant call for applications as early as possible and allow sufficient time to obtain academic documents, prepare application materials and complete any university-specific requirements. Programmes Not Currently Open It is also important to distinguish between programmes that are currently accepting applications and programmes that the DAAD database indicates will be published later. The current database identifies the following programmes as expected to be published in spring 2027 : Master of Science in Physics — Federal University of Agriculture Abeokuta, Nigeria Master of Philosophy in Urban Studies – Southern Urbanism — University of Cape Town, South Africa Master of Science in Mathematics — University of Pretoria, South Africa Applicants interested in these programmes should monitor future DAAD announcements rather than attempting to apply through the current open calls. How to Find the Correct Call for Applications The DAAD scholarship database provides a separate call for applications for each participating degree programme. For example, applicants interested in the University of Ghana s WACCI programme should consult the specific call for the Master of Philosophy in Seed Science and Technology , while applicants interested in WACCBIP should consult the separate call for Master of Philosophy in Molecular Cell Biology of Infectious Diseases . This programme-specific approach is important because the exact admission requirements, application instructions and selection procedures may vary. Applicants should therefore avoid treating the general scholarship database page as a substitute for the detailed programme call. A Strong Opportunity for Future African Researchers and University Educators One of the most important features of the DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme is its emphasis on applicants who intend to pursue careers in teaching and/or research at higher education institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa . This makes the opportunity particularly relevant for graduates who see postgraduate education as part of a longer-term academic or research career. For example, a Master s degree supported through this programme could provide an academic foundation for someone seeking to develop expertise in agricultural research, environmental science, climate studies, engineering, education research, public health or other development-related fields. The programme therefore connects postgraduate education with the broader objective of developing African knowledge institutions. Visit HERE to find the full details about the DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme Sub-Saharan Africa 2026–2027. Conclusion The DAAD In-Country/In-Region Programme Sub-Saharan Africa 2026–2027 provides an important opportunity for graduates from Sub-Saharan Africa to pursue selected development-related Master s degrees while remaining within Africa. With funding generally covering the regular duration of the Master s programme, usually up to two years, successful scholars can receive a monthly scholarship, study and research support, thesis publishing costs and tuition support. In-Region scholars may additionally receive travel support and health insurance. The current programme includes Master s opportunities in areas such as water and environmental engineering, seed science and technology, molecular cell biology, agricultural economics, environmental health, plant breeding, education research, electrical power systems, geomatics, climate change and disaster management, aquaculture and fisheries science, and irrigation engineering . The programme also places particular emphasis on strengthening higher education systems in Sub-Saharan Africa and encourages applications from women, recognised refugees, and candidates from marginalised regions or groups . Most importantly, applicants should remember that the general DAAD scholarship page is only the starting point. Each participating university and degree programme has its own detailed call for applications, and applicants must follow the specific instructions applicable to their chosen programme. The application deadline for the currently open opportunities is November 12, 2026. Prospective applicants should begin preparing early, carefully review the relevant programme-specific call, confirm their eligibility and submit a complete application before the deadline. title: Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program 2027: Paid Public Policy Fellowship at the University of Delaware
summary: The Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program 2027 at the University of Delaware offers students an opportunity to gain practical experience inside the legislative and public policy process while working directly with the Delaware General Assembly . Managed by the University of Delaware’s Institute for Public Administration , the program connects the research capacity of the University of Delaware and Delaware State University with the research needs of the Delaware General Assembly. Since its establishment in 1982, the program has provided selected students with the opportunity to observe governmental decision-making and contribute research that can assist legislators in addressing important public policy issues. For students interested in public policy, political science, government, public administration, international relations, economics, communications, criminal justice, sociology, urban affairs, history, or business administration , the Legislative Fellows Program provides a practical opportunity to connect academic knowledge with real-world policymaking. The 2027 program is particularly relevant for students who want to develop their research, writing, communication, policy analysis, and professional networking skills while gaining first-hand exposure to the workings of state government. What Is the Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program? The Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program is a competitive student fellowship designed to place qualified students in direct contact with the legislative process in Delaware. The program was begun in 1982 and is administered by the University of Delaware’s Institute for Public Administration. Fellows conduct nonpartisan, in-depth research on important issues affecting the state and provide research support to legislators and legislative staff. Rather than being purely classroom-based, the fellowship gives students the opportunity to experience how public policy is developed and implemented in practice. In recent years, Legislative Fellows have contributed to research on a range of significant public policy issues, including: Criminal justice reform Healthcare Government accountability Government transparency Women’s rights Other critical issues affecting Delaware This means that participants are not simply studying government from an academic perspective. They have the opportunity to contribute research and analysis that can inform actual legislative work. What Makes the 2027 Legislative Fellows Program Valuable? The program provides a direct connection between academic study and public service. Students selected as Fellows can develop an understanding of how legislative institutions operate, how policy questions are researched, and how evidence and analysis can be communicated to policymakers. According to the University of Delaware, Fellows have the opportunity to: Affect current legislation by providing timely, nonpartisan and in-depth information on critical issues. Develop professional relationships with important state leaders in both the legislative and executive branches. Gain an understanding of the legislative process that can be useful in public, nonprofit and private-sector careers. The experience can therefore be valuable even for students who do not ultimately intend to become politicians or work permanently in government. Understanding how public-sector institutions function can strengthen careers in research, advocacy, nonprofit organizations, consulting, communications, business, public administration and other fields. Paid Legislative Fellowship Opportunity The 2027 Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program is a paid fellowship program . Fellows will work directly with legislators and legislative staff while conducting research and supporting legislative committees. The practical nature of the program makes it particularly valuable for students who want to build experience beyond traditional academic coursework. Participants will also take a three-credit seminar, State Government: Management and Policy , which provides an academic component that allows students to connect their legislative experiences with university coursework. This combination of practical legislative work and academic study gives Fellows an opportunity to understand both the theoretical and practical dimensions of government and public policy. What Will Legislative Fellows Do? Selected Fellows will work with legislators and legislative staff and participate in research and committee-related activities. For the 2027 program, Fellows are scheduled to work in Dover on: Tuesdays Wednesdays Thursdays The fellowship activities will take place from January 12 through June 30, 2027 . An orientation is scheduled for the first full week of January . The program will expose students to the day-to-day realities of legislative work, including policy research, committee activities and interactions with government officials. Travel to Dover For Fellows travelling from the University of Delaware campus, transportation to Dover is provided through a vanpool, subject to conditions. According to the program information, Fellows will leave campus at approximately 11:00 a.m. and return at approximately 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. This arrangement is designed to facilitate participation in the legislative program while providing transportation between the University of Delaware campus and Dover. Academic Component of the Fellowship One distinctive feature of the Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program is that the practical experience is connected to academic coursework. Fellows take a three-credit seminar titled State Government: Management and Policy . The seminar provides an opportunity for students to reflect on and connect their practical experiences with academic concepts related to state government, management and public policy. For students studying public administration, political science, public policy and related disciplines, this academic component can provide an important bridge between classroom learning and professional experience. Who Can Apply for the 2027 Legislative Fellows Program? The University of Delaware states that eligibility is open to: Full-time master s degree students; or Especially qualified junior- or senior-level undergraduate students with a GPA of 3.4 or higher ; Students must be from the partnering universities . Applicants should have a strong background in relevant academic fields, including: Public administration Public policy Political science Sociology Urban affairs Communications International relations Criminal justice History Economics Business administration The program also indicates that applicants with an interest in the legislative process, government or public policy analysis are preferred. Strong writing skills are required. Because the source specifically refers to students from the partnering universities, applicants should carefully confirm their institutional eligibility before preparing an application. Academic Requirements One of the clearest academic requirements stated by the University of Delaware is the 3.4 GPA minimum for especially qualified junior- and senior-level undergraduate applicants . Full-time master s students are also eligible to apply. Beyond GPA, the program places emphasis on applicants academic background and demonstrated ability to engage with policy-related issues. A strong academic foundation in a relevant discipline can therefore help applicants demonstrate their suitability for the fellowship. Important Skills for Applicants The program is designed around research, policy analysis and communication. Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate strong analytical and writing abilities. The University of Delaware specifically states that strong writing skills are required . Applicants with an interest in the legislative process, government or public policy analysis are preferred. Students preparing to apply should therefore be ready to demonstrate their ability to: Research complex issues Analyze public policy questions Write clearly and accurately Present evidence-based arguments Understand government institutions Communicate research findings Work with policymakers and legislative staff Meet deadlines Work professionally in a public-sector environment Competitive Selection Process The Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program is competitive. Candidates are interviewed, and applicants must complete a timed-writing exercise based on a current public policy issue . The official application process consists of four stages: 1. Application and Supporting Documents Applicants begin by submitting the application and the required supporting documentation. 2. Writing Exercise Candidates complete a timed writing exercise focused on a current public policy issue. This component is particularly important because the fellowship involves producing research and written information for legislators and legislative staff. 3. Initial Interview Candidates who progress through the process participate in an initial interview. 4. Panel Interview The final stage involves a panel interview. Students should therefore prepare for both written and oral evaluation during the selection process. Professional Networking Opportunities The fellowship provides students with opportunities to develop professional relationships with government officials and community leaders. According to the University of Delaware, Fellows can make important contacts with government officials and community leaders while expanding their professional networks. This networking component can be particularly valuable for students considering careers in: Government Public administration Public policy Legislative affairs Nonprofit organizations International relations Communications Research Advocacy Consulting Public-sector management The program can therefore serve as an important bridge between university study and professional public service. Click HERE to register for an information session. Exposure to Delaware s Government and Legislative Process A major advantage of the fellowship is the opportunity to observe how policymaking takes place in practice. Students can become acquainted with important leaders in Delaware s General Assembly and executive branch and develop a better understanding of the legislative process. This experience can help students understand how policy ideas move from research and debate into legislative decision-making. It can also expose participants to the practical challenges policymakers face when dealing with complex issues affecting communities. Research Experience in Public Policy The fellowship emphasizes nonpartisan, in-depth research . This is significant because Fellows are expected to contribute research that can assist legislators in addressing critical issues rather than approaching their work primarily from a partisan perspective. Past areas of research have included criminal justice reform, healthcare, government accountability and transparency, and women s rights. Students therefore gain experience in researching real-world policy problems and communicating useful information to decision-makers. How the Fellowship Can Strengthen a Student s Career Participation in the Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program can provide several forms of professional development. Policy Research Skills Students gain practical experience researching current public policy issues and producing information that can be useful to policymakers. Legislative Process Knowledge Participants gain first-hand exposure to the workings of a state legislature and the governmental decision-making process. Professional Writing The program requires strong writing skills and includes a timed-writing exercise during selection. Fellows research responsibilities also provide opportunities to strengthen policy writing. Communication Skills Working with legislators, legislative staff, government officials and community leaders can strengthen professional communication. Networking Fellows have opportunities to build contacts with government officials and community leaders. Public-Service Experience Students gain practical exposure to government operations and public-sector work. Transferable Career Skills The University of Delaware notes that understanding the legislative process can be useful across public, nonprofit and private-sector careers. Learn More HERE Fellowship Schedule for 2027 The 2027 program will run during the spring legislative session. Key dates and activities include: First full week of January 2027: Orientation January 12, 2027: Legislative Fellowship activities begin January 12–June 30, 2027: Fellows work with legislators and legislative staff on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays June 30, 2027: Scheduled end of the fellowship activities 2027: Fellows also participate in the three-credit State Government: Management and Policy seminar The program s schedule is designed to integrate legislative work with students academic experience. Application Deadline for the 2027 Program The application deadline for the spring 2027 Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program is Friday, October 30, 2026 . Students interested in applying should not wait until the final day to begin preparing. Because the selection process includes supporting documents, a timed-writing exercise and interviews, applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare. How to Prepare for the Application Students interested in the program can strengthen their preparation by focusing on several areas. Review Current Public Policy Issues Since applicants must complete a timed writing exercise on a current public policy issue, candidates should become familiar with major policy debates and learn how to analyze an issue from an evidence-based perspective. Strengthen Policy Writing Applicants should practice writing clear, structured responses under time constraints. A strong policy response should generally: Clearly identify the policy problem. Explain why the issue matters. Present relevant evidence. Consider different perspectives. Analyze possible policy responses. Present a clear and balanced conclusion. Understand the Legislative Process Applicants should develop a basic understanding of how legislatures operate, how committees function and how policymakers use research and evidence. Highlight Relevant Academic Experience Students should emphasize coursework, research projects, papers, internships, community engagement or other experiences that demonstrate their interest in government and public policy. Prepare for Interviews Because candidates are interviewed during the selection process, applicants should be prepared to explain: Why they are interested in the fellowship Why public policy matters to them What policy issues interest them How their academic background prepares them for the program What they hope to learn How they would contribute as a Legislative Fellow Click HERE to APPLY Why Students Interested in Public Policy Should Consider This Fellowship Many students learn about government and policymaking primarily through lectures, textbooks and academic research. The Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program provides an opportunity to take that knowledge into an actual governmental environment. The fellowship allows students to see how research is used in legislative decision-making and how policymakers respond to complex social and economic issues. It can also help students understand that public policy is not simply about political debate. Effective policymaking requires research, evidence, communication, analysis, collaboration and an understanding of the needs of communities. For students considering long-term careers in public service, this type of practical experience can be particularly valuable. Examples of Career Areas Relevant to the Fellowship The experience gained through the program may be relevant to careers in: Public policy analysis Legislative affairs Government administration Public administration Political research Policy research Nonprofit management Advocacy Communications International relations Government relations Community development Research and evaluation Public-sector consulting Social policy The University of Delaware specifically notes that the understanding of the legislative process gained through the fellowship can be useful in public, nonprofit and private-sector careers. Previous Fellows Experiences The program s previous Fellows have highlighted the practical value of the experience. Former Legislative Fellow Lexi West described the opportunity to research issues across state lines, develop recommendations for legislators and strengthen planning, communication and organizational skills. Scott Murphy Eisenhart, a former Legislative Fellow, emphasized the value of observing how policymaking unfolds in the real world. Another former Fellow, Brandon Grabelsky, highlighted the development of writing and policy research skills and the ability to produce high-quality work under short deadlines. These reflections demonstrate that the program is intended not merely as an academic exercise but as a practical professional development opportunity. Where Is the Program Based? The Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program is connected to the University of Delaware and the Delaware General Assembly . Legislative work takes place in Dover, Delaware , with transportation arrangements from the University of Delaware campus described in the program information. The University of Delaware is located in Newark, Delaware, USA . Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity may be particularly suitable for students who are interested in understanding government from the inside and developing practical policy research experience. Potentially relevant students include those studying: Public administration Public policy Political science Sociology Urban affairs Communications International relations Criminal justice History Economics Business administration However, the official eligibility requirement specifies that applicants must be full-time master s students or especially qualified junior- or senior-level undergraduate students from the partnering universities. Important Information Before Applying Prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the institutional eligibility requirement. The University of Delaware source does not describe this as an open worldwide fellowship. Instead, it specifically states that eligible students are from the partnering universities . Therefore, students should confirm that their university is one of the participating institutions before investing significant time in preparing an application. Applicants should also remember that selection is competitive and involves both written and interview components. Application Deadline The deadline for the 2027 Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program is Friday, October 30, 2026 . Interested students should begin preparing early, particularly because the selection process includes supporting documents, a timed writing exercise, an initial interview and a panel interview. Visit HERE for more information about the Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program 2027. Conclusion The Jerome R. Lewis Legislative Fellows Program 2027 offers a distinctive opportunity for qualified students to move beyond classroom discussions of government and experience the legislative process directly. Through paid legislative work, nonpartisan policy research, interaction with legislators and government officials, professional networking and a three-credit academic seminar, Fellows can develop practical skills that are valuable across government, nonprofit and private-sector careers. For eligible students, the fellowship can provide an opportunity to understand how policy research is translated into governmental decision-making, strengthen professional writing and analytical skills, build relationships with public-sector leaders and gain first-hand experience in the workings of state government. Students who meet the requirements and are interested in the 2027 legislative session should take note of the October 30, 2026 application deadline and begin preparing well in advance of the selection process. title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development 2027–2029: Scholarships to Study Across Europe
summary: The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development (ILSPSD) is a two-year international master s programme designed for students who want to develop advanced expertise at the intersection of international law, security, peace, sustainability, politics and global governance . The programme brings together six European degree-awarding higher education institutions and a wider network of 30 associate partners to prepare the next generation of international lawyers, policymakers and professionals capable of addressing complex global challenges. For the 2027–2029 intake , prospective students can apply either for an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) Scholarship or as self-funded students . The scholarship application deadline is 4 January 2027 at 23:59 CET , while self-funded applications remain open until 31 March 2027 at 23:59 CEST . The programme is particularly distinctive because students do not remain at a single university throughout their studies. Instead, mobility is central to the programme, with students studying in three or more countries over 24 months and completing different components of the programme at participating European institutions. What Is the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development? The ILSPSD programme was established in response to the increasingly interconnected challenges facing the international community. Contemporary global challenges such as armed conflict, terrorism, forced migration, climate change, biodiversity loss, hybrid threats and democratic backsliding often overlap rather than occur independently. The programme describes these interconnected challenges as contributing to a global polycrisis that creates significant challenges for security, peace and sustainable development. Addressing such challenges requires professionals who can understand more than one dimension of an international problem. For example, a contemporary conflict may involve: International and domestic law Human rights Security concerns Political institutions International organizations Migration and displacement Environmental pressures Economic development Sustainability Global governance The ILSPSD programme therefore adopts a multidisciplinary approach that combines international law with politics, sustainability and security studies . Its objective is to equip students with the knowledge and analytical skills required to understand and contribute to solutions for complex global problems. A Two-Year International Master s Programme The ILSPSD is a 24-month, full-time master s programme with an October intake. One of its defining features is international mobility. Rather than completing the entire degree at one institution, students move between participating European universities as they progress through different stages of the curriculum. According to the programme, students study in three or more countries during the 24-month programme . This structure allows students to experience different academic environments, legal traditions, policy perspectives and European contexts. For students interested in international careers, the mobility component can also provide an opportunity to develop an international professional and academic network. The Six European Degree-Awarding Universities The programme is delivered through a consortium of six European degree-awarding partner institutions . The participating universities are: Leuphana University of Lüneburg, Germany Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals (IBEI), Spain University of Glasgow, United Kingdom Université libre de Bruxelles, Belgium Universidade NOVA de Lisboa, Portugal University of Tartu, Estonia The programme also has a network of 30 associate partners , extending its academic and professional connections beyond the six degree-awarding institutions. The participating institutions bring different academic strengths and international perspectives to the joint programme. How the ILSPSD Programme Is Structured The programme begins at Leuphana University of Lüneburg , where students study International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development through either an LL.M. or M.A. study track . Students then continue to the Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals , where they study Theories of International Security . After this foundation, students choose from four specialization tracks. 1. International Law and International Security This specialization is offered at the University of Glasgow . It is designed for students who want to deepen their understanding of the relationship between international law and international security. 2. Security and Conflict This track is offered at the Université libre de Bruxelles . It provides an opportunity to focus more closely on issues surrounding security and conflict. 3. Globalization, Law and Security This specialization is offered at Universidade NOVA de Lisboa . It provides a focus on the relationship between globalization, law and security in an increasingly interconnected world. 4. International Law and Human Rights This specialization is offered at the University of Tartu . Students choosing this pathway can develop deeper expertise in international law and human rights. The four tracks give students an opportunity to shape their studies according to their academic interests and professional ambitions. Final Semester: Research Dissertation and Work Placement The final semester of the programme is dedicated to a research dissertation . Students also have the option of completing a work placement , providing an opportunity to connect their academic training with practical professional experience. The dissertation component allows students to undertake independent research on an issue related to the programme s broader areas of law, security, peace and sustainable development. For students planning careers in research, academia, policy analysis or international organizations, this research component can be particularly valuable. Practical and Experiential Learning The ILSPSD programme extends beyond traditional classroom teaching. Students can benefit from several practical and experiential learning opportunities, including: Summer schools Legal clinics Guest lectures Direct interaction with practitioners Optional work placements International academic mobility Research dissertation work These activities are designed to complement formal academic study with practical exposure to professional environments. The programme therefore combines academic knowledge with opportunities to engage with professionals and real-world issues. An Interdisciplinary Approach to Global Challenges One of the strongest features of the ILSPSD programme is its interdisciplinary structure. International problems rarely fit neatly within one academic discipline. A security crisis may have legal, political, economic, environmental and humanitarian dimensions. The programme consequently integrates: International law International security Peace studies Politics Sustainability Human rights Globalization Conflict studies Global governance The programme describes its approach as a holistic combination of law, politics, security and sustainability , supported by international mobility and hands-on experience. This interdisciplinary foundation can be particularly useful for students who want to work on complex international issues rather than specialize exclusively in one narrow field. Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Opportunity The ILSPSD programme offers applicants the opportunity to apply for an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship for the 2027–2029 intake. The programme website states that there are 70 Erasmus Mundus scholarships associated with the programme. Applicants can choose between applying for the scholarship route or applying as self-funded students. The two routes have different application deadlines. EMJM Scholarship Deadline The application platform for the 2027–2029 intake with an EMJM Scholarship is open until: 4 January 2027 at 23:59 CET. Self-Funded Application Deadline Students who intend to fund their studies themselves can apply until: 31 March 2027 at 23:59 CEST. Applicants interested in scholarship funding should therefore pay particular attention to the earlier January deadline. What Students Can Gain From the Programme The ILSPSD programme is designed to prepare graduates for careers that require an understanding of international law, global security, peace and sustainable development. The programme identifies potential career pathways including: International courts International organizations European Union institutions Government ministries Government agencies Non-governmental organizations Think tanks International policy environments Other organizations involved in global affairs Graduates can develop multidisciplinary expertise, practical experience and an international professional network. The programme s emphasis on the intersection of law, security, peace and sustainability can therefore be relevant to students interested in international careers. International Mobility and Global Networking International mobility is not simply an additional feature of ILSPSD; it is central to the programme. Students study in at least three countries during their two years and interact with students, academics and practitioners from different backgrounds. This can help students develop: Cross-cultural communication skills International academic networks Exposure to different legal and political systems Understanding of European and international policy environments Professional connections across countries Adaptability in different academic and cultural settings For students seeking careers in international organizations, diplomacy, global policy or international law, such exposure can be particularly relevant. The Six Partner Universities Leuphana University of Lüneburg Leuphana University of Lüneburg is located in Germany and is described by the programme as a modern, innovative and internationally oriented university. It serves as the starting point for the programme s academic journey. Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals The Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals, or IBEI, is presented as an internationally recognized academic and research centre. Students study Theories of International Security at this institution during the programme. University of Glasgow The University of Glasgow hosts the International Law and International Security specialization. Its international law school has a long academic history and teaches students from more than 140 countries. Université libre de Bruxelles The Université libre de Bruxelles hosts the Security and Conflict specialization. The university is described as multicultural, with approximately one-third of its students and researchers coming from abroad. Universidade NOVA de Lisboa Universidade NOVA de Lisboa hosts the Globalization, Law and Security specialization. The university emphasizes creative teaching and research and aims to create value for society. University of Tartu The University of Tartu hosts the International Law and Human Rights specialization. Established in 1632, it is described by the programme as Estonia s leading centre for research and training. Who Should Consider the ILSPSD Programme? The programme is particularly relevant for prospective master s students who are interested in the relationship between law, security, peace and sustainable development. Potential applicants may be interested in areas such as: International law International security Human rights Peace and conflict International relations Global governance Sustainable development International politics European affairs Security studies Diplomacy Policy development The programme s multidisciplinary structure means that students interested in the broader relationship between legal, political and security systems may find it especially relevant. Preparing for the Application The programme strongly advises prospective students to read the Step-by-Step Application Guide carefully before starting their application. Applicants should therefore avoid beginning the application process without first reviewing the official instructions. A sensible preparation process includes: Reviewing the programme structure and specialization tracks. Understanding the difference between the scholarship and self-funded application routes. Reviewing the entry requirements. Studying the application guide carefully. Identifying the specialization that best matches academic and career goals. Preparing application materials well before the deadline. Checking the appropriate deadline for the intended funding route. Submitting the application through the designated platform. Students seeking the Erasmus Mundus Scholarship should particularly prioritize the 4 January 2027 deadline because the self-funded deadline is later. Scholarship Applicants Should Plan Early The EMJM Scholarship deadline is significantly earlier than the self-funded application deadline. This creates an important distinction for applicants: Scholarship applicants : 4 January 2027, 23:59 CET Self-funded applicants : 31 March 2027, 23:59 CEST Students who need financial support should therefore not assume that they can wait until the March deadline. The January deadline is the relevant date for the EMJM Scholarship application. A Programme Designed for the Future of Global Governance The challenges facing the international community are increasingly interconnected. Conflict can influence migration. Climate change can intensify resource pressures. Political instability can affect development. Environmental degradation can create security concerns. Technological and hybrid threats can create new challenges for states and international institutions. The ILSPSD programme is designed around precisely this type of interconnected problem. By bringing together law, security, politics and sustainability, the programme seeks to prepare students to understand complex global challenges and contribute to solutions. The programme s emphasis on training the next generation of lawyers and policymakers reflects its broader objective of developing professionals who can operate across disciplinary and national boundaries. Career Prospects After Graduation Graduates can use the knowledge and experience gained from ILSPSD in a range of international and policy-oriented careers. Potential professional environments include: International Courts and Legal Institutions Students specializing in international law and human rights may find the programme relevant to careers involving international legal institutions and related organizations. International Organizations The programme s focus on global governance, peace, security and sustainable development can provide relevant preparation for work in international organizations. European Union Institutions The programme s European mobility and focus on international governance can be useful for students interested in European policy and institutional environments. Government Ministries and Agencies Graduates may apply their policy, legal and analytical skills in government ministries and agencies working on foreign affairs, security, development, justice or related policy areas. NGOs and Civil Society Organizations Organizations working on human rights, peacebuilding, conflict, migration, sustainability and international development can also benefit from professionals with interdisciplinary expertise. Think Tanks and Research Organizations The research dissertation and analytical foundation can provide useful preparation for policy research and think-tank environments. The programme itself identifies international courts and organizations, the EU, ministries, government agencies, NGOs and think tanks among the potential professional destinations for graduates. Students applying as self-funded candidates have until 31 March 2027 at 23:59 CEST . The programme specifically advises applicants to carefully read the Step-by-Step Application Guide before beginning the application. APPLY HERE Conclusion The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development 2027–2029 offers an international and multidisciplinary master s experience for students interested in the increasingly important relationship between law, peace, security and sustainable development . Its structure distinguishes it from a conventional master s programme. Students study across three or more European countries , begin their academic journey at Leuphana University of Lüneburg, continue at the Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals, and then specialize at one of four partner universities in Glasgow, Brussels, Lisbon or Tartu. Beyond academic coursework, the programme incorporates research, legal clinics, summer schools, guest lectures, practitioner engagement and an optional work placement. Students also complete a research dissertation during their final semester. With 70 Erasmus Mundus scholarships available through the programme and an application deadline of 4 January 2027 at 23:59 CET for scholarship applicants, prospective students who require financial support should begin preparing early. Self-funded applicants have a later deadline of 31 March 2027 at 23:59 CEST . For aspiring international lawyers, policymakers, researchers and professionals interested in global affairs, the ILSPSD programme provides an opportunity to build multidisciplinary expertise, gain international academic experience and develop networks across Europe.
